Formal statement: If Eq(A) has equivalence classes B_1,…,B_c with |B_j|=m_j, its adjacency matrix is permutation-similar to diag(J_{m_1},…,J_{m_c}).
Proof: An equivalence relation contains every pair within a class and no pair between classes.

Formal statement: For a class of size m, L(K_m)=mI_m−J_m has spectrum {0, m^(m−1)}.
Proof: J_m has eigenvalue m on 1 and 0 on its orthogonal complement.
Each block contributes m_j−1 nonzero eigenvalues.
Each connected clique block contributes one zero mode.

Formal statement: For permutation matrix P, L' = P L P^T.

Proof: Similar matrices have identical characteristic polynomials.
Functional calculus preserves similarity: e^{-tL'}=P e^{-tL}P^T; trace is cyclic.

Formal statement: If Γ_A and Γ_B have identical terminal Eq(A) semantics and use the same graph extraction rule, then their Laplacian spectra and heat traces are identical; under different vertex labels they remain permutation-similar.
Proof: F1 fixes the terminal relation; L1–T6 propagate equivalence through the descent.
